As of 310 PM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Overcast, breezy, and unsettled conditions continue 
this evening into Thursday.

This afternoon, latest analysis shows a classic cold air 
damming/wedge set up over the region. Strong, 1040+ mb high pressure 
is currently centered over eastern Canada into the New England 
states and is ridging southward. Meanwhile, coastal low pressure 
(currently ~1012 mb) is currently taking shape well offshore. The 
resulting tightening pressure gradient between the two features is 
driving strong N/NE flow across the region. Latest radar and surface 
observations show widespread drizzle and rain showers across the 
local area and overcast skies. Temperatures range from the mid to 
upper 50s across western portions of the forecast area, to the upper 
60s to lower 70s across the southeast. Wind gusts along the 
immediate coast have been gusting to 35 to 45 mph this afternoon, 
and a few localized gusts of 50 mph are possible later this evening 
into tonight. A Wind Advisory remains in effect for the coastal 
counties through Thursday. Rain slowly diminishes in coverage this 
evening and transitions to light showers/drizzle/mist. Low 
temperatures tonight will range from the lower to mid 50s NW/W to 
the lower to mid 60s SE. 

The coastal low will slowly begin to make its trek E/NE during the 
day on Thursday allowing for high pressure to begin to build back 
into the area. The pressure gradient will remain tight along the 
coast, allowing for wind gusts of 40 to 45+ mph to continue. The 
best rain chances tomorrow will be across far E and SE portions of 
the forecast area as moisture wrap around the coastal low. 
Otherwise, overcast skies, cool temperatures, and areas of 
drizzle/mist will continue as we remain in the wedge. The wedge 
begins to weaken later in the day on Thursday, and a few peaks of 
sunshine will be possible across far N/NW portions of the area. High 
temperatures on Thursday will range from the lower to mid 60s NW to 
the lower 70s SE. Low temperatures Thursday night drop back into the 
upper 40s to lower 50s for many areas west of I-95 as we begin to 
see some clearing work into the area. Closer to the coast, lows 
range from the mid 50s to lower 60s. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Drier and warmer conditions return Friday into the 
weekend. Remaining breezy into the weekend along the immediate coast.

Afternoon models still show some disagreement in regards to the
timing and future track of the coastal low Friday into the 
weekend. The ECMWF remains slower with the low and ultimately 
tracks it closer to the coast, eventually stalling the low off 
the NJ coast Saturday night into Sunday. The GFS is faster and 
further east with the low track, eventually stalling the low 
near Cape Cod on Sunday. The ECMWF solution would allow for 
continued rain chances across NE portions of the area into the 
weekend. The ECMWF is the outlier amongst the model guidance 
right now. For now, the NBM solution is closer to the GFS which 
keeps the low east and is also faster. This allows for a mainly 
sunny and dry weekend with temperatures rebounding back into the
70s. It will still remain breezy along the immediate coast at 
least into Saturday, before gradually diminishing Saturday night
into Sunday. High pressure builds into the area early next week
allowing for dry conditions and mild temperatures. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...Widespread moderate to locally major tidal 
flooding (inundation of 2-3 feet AGL in vulnerable areas) is likely 
by this afternoon/evening high tide due to strong northeast winds. 
Tidal flooding is expected to continue for several tide cycles given 
the persistent northeast winds.

Northeast winds continue to persist 25-30 kt with gusts to 35-40 kt 
this afternoon. These wind are likely to persist through Thursday 
before gradually becoming N then NNW by Friday and Saturday while 
diminishing slightly (especially across the bay and rivers). Tidal 
anomalies continue to remain ~2.5 ft above normal across the middle 
and lower bay and will continue to rise through Thursday. 
(especially along the bay, tidal rivers, and Atlantic coast).
Widespread moderate to major flooding is expected for the 3 high 
tide cycles from this evening through the Thursday evening/night 
high tide. Some sites (especially Jamestown/Lynnhaven/Smithfield) 
could crest around 0.5 ft above major flood stage. Coastal Flood 
Warnings remain in effect for nearly the entire tidal area through 
Thursday night/Friday morning. There continues to remain some 
uncertainty with respect to the forecast on Friday and Saturday as 
winds become N-NNW and there is a weak signal of some possible 
ebbing. ETSS still shows moderate flooding in the lower bay and
